title: Expansion Incentive Matrix and Security Questionnaire Integration for Enterprise Renewals
creator: Ava Martinez
description:
Problem statement: Enterprise customers currently negotiate multi-year discounts and true-ups ad hoc, which creates friction during renewals, slows closings, and occasionally exposes us to long-term underpricing when growth runs ahead of contract terms. Sales needs a repeatable, defensible framework that speeds negotiations, ties discounts to measurable commitments, and reduces security questionnaire (SQ) turnaround as a gating factor for multi-year incentives.

Goal: Define an 'Expansion Incentive Matrix' that standardizes multi-year discounts, tiered true-up windows, and uplift rules for in-term expansion, and integrate SQ/SSO readiness as a part of the renewal checklist so security gating does not block incentive eligibility. The matrix should be experimentable (A/B by cohort) and instrumentable for NRR/ARR/pricing leakage metrics.

Scope: 1) Design discount tiers for 1-, 2-, and 3-year contracts with clear true-up cadence (quarterly vs annual), 2) Define uplift rules when annualized usage grows >25% or >50% within a term (automatic pro-rata true-up + discount reduction path), 3) Define minimum compliance/security milestones required for full incentive eligibility (e.g., completed SQ with acceptable exceptions OR SSO + SCIM enabled + encryption-in-transit validated), 4) Integration plan with Renewals workflow (Salesforce + renewal ops playbooks + Console renewal banner), 5) Instrumentation plan for measuring revenue impact and sales velocity.

Out of scope: Wholesale changes to pricing list or creation of new SKUs. No changes to core billing engine for this experiment (we will use true-up invoicing patterns we already support).
acceptance_criteria:
1) A defined incentive matrix document reviewed by Finance, Legal, Security, and Sales ops.
2) A renewal checklist that marks 'security milestone' and ties to discount eligibility.
3) Instrumentation added to renewal flow to capture cohort, discount offered, true-up schedule, and final ARR outcome.
4) Pilot the incentive matrix with 15 enterprise renewals in Q2 and report NRR and average time-to-close delta.
5) Legal sign-off on standard contract rider language for 2- and 3-year commitments.
experiment_design:
Cohorts: randomize eligible renewals (by ARR band and region) into Control (current ad-hoc commercial) vs Experiment (matrix + expedited SQ path).
Metrics: primary: Net Revenue Retention (90d and 12mo), secondary: time-to-close (days), discount depth as percent of list, percent of deals requiring contract rider changes, SQ turnaround time.
Size: target 15 pilot deals across small (50-250k ARR), mid (250-1M), and large (>1M) segments.
Duration: 12 weeks pilot with weekly checkpoints.
Analysis plan: pre/post cohort comparison; surface confounders (renewal executive, existing discount history).
tradeoffs:
- Revenue protection vs. sales velocity: deeper, standard discounts shorten negotiation but increase near-term revenue loss if customers under-commit.
- Security strictness vs. incentive uptake: stricter SQ requirements reduce incentive eligibility and may push customers toward shorter terms.
- Complexity vs. adoption: a matrix with too many carveouts will be ignored by Sales. We favor a simpler 3x3 matrix (term length x ARR band) with two uplift breakpoints.
- Implementation speed vs. legal rigor: to pilot quickly we will use contract rider templates; a fully embedded T&Cs update will defer to Q3.
